name: Tenofovir disoproxil
drug_class: Nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NtRTI; acyclic adenosine phosphonate prodrug)
route_note: oral tablet once daily, alone or in fixed-dose combinations
originator: Antonín Holý (IOCB Prague) and Erik De Clercq (Rega Institute, Leuven); developed by Gilead Sciences

discovery.by: Antonín Holý and Erik De Clercq, with Gilead Sciences
discovery.note: Tenofovir (PMPA) is an acyclic nucleoside phosphonate; the disoproxil ester prodrug was made to allow oral absorption.

tagline: Backbone of HIV treatment and prevention, and first-line therapy for hepatitis B
summary: Tenofovir disoproxil is an oral prodrug of tenofovir, a nucleotide analogue that blocks HIV reverse transcriptase and the hepatitis B virus polymerase. Combined with emtricitabine or lamivudine it forms the backbone of many HIV regimens and of oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). Long-term use can affect kidney function and bone density.
mechanism: Tenofovir disoproxil is hydrolysed in the gut and blood to tenofovir, which already carries a phosphonate group and so needs only two phosphorylation steps by cellular kinases to form tenofovir diphosphate.

Tenofovir diphosphate competes with deoxyadenosine triphosphate for HIV reverse transcriptase and HBV polymerase and terminates the DNA chain after incorporation. The K65R mutation in HIV reverse transcriptase reduces susceptibility; HBV resistance to tenofovir is very rare.
uses: HIV-1 infection in combination with other antiretrovirals
Chronic hepatitis B in adults and children
Prevention of mother-to-child HBV transmission (guideline use in pregnancy)

history.title: Antiviral activity
history.detail: Holý and De Clercq report the activity of PMPA against retroviruses; Gilead has licensed their phosphonate compounds.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Viread is approved for HIV-1 infection.

history.title: Truvada
history.detail: The fixed-dose combination with emtricitabine (Truvada) is approved.

history.title: Atripla
history.detail: Efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil becomes the first once-daily single-tablet HIV regimen.

history.title: Hepatitis B
history.detail: Viread is approved for chronic hepatitis B.

history.title: PrEP
history.detail: Truvada becomes the first drug approved for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis, after the iPrEx and Partners PrEP trials.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic tenofovir disoproxil enters the US market; generic Truvada follows in 2020.

pk.half_life: plasma tenofovir about 17 h; intracellular diphosphate much longer
pk.bioavailability: about 25% fasting, higher with a high-fat meal
pk.metabolism: esterase hydrolysis to tenofovir; not a CYP substrate
pk.excretion: renal (glomerular filtration and active tubular secretion via OAT1/OAT3)

serious: new or worsening renal impairment, including Fanconi syndrome
safety.boxed_warning: Severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B in patients co-infected with HBV who discontinue the drug (US label).

facts: Tenofovir royalties made the Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry in Prague one of the best-funded research institutes in central Europe.
Tenofovir/emtricitabine was the first approved HIV PrEP regimen.
Tenofovir disoproxil is part of the WHO-preferred TLD regimen (tenofovir/lamivudine/dolutegravir).

references.title: Grant RM et al. Preexposure chemoprophylaxis for HIV prevention in men who have sex with men (iPrEx). NEJM 2010
